title: New York Times bars photographers from Photoshop 2027 over hidden AI risk
summary: The New York Times bans Photoshop 2027 for photographers over AI metadata risks
detailed: A photographer preparing a news image for The New York Times can use an older version of Photoshop, but must avoid version 28.0.0 and its subsequent updates on assignment for the paper.
Times spokesperson Graham James confirmed the instruction to PetaPixel on 24 November.
The Times says some tools can use generative AI without making that clear to the photographer.
If one is used, the file can carry an AI disclosure even when the contributor thought they were making an ordinary correction.
sentences: A photographer preparing a news image for The New York Times can use an older version of Photoshop, but must avoid version 28.0.0 and its subsequent updates on assignment for the paper.
Times spokesperson Graham James confirmed the instruction to PetaPixel on 24 November.
The problem for a picture editor is what happens between taking the photograph and filing it.
The Times says some tools can use generative AI without making that clear to the photographer.
If one is used, the file can carry an AI disclosure even when the contributor thought they were making an ordinary correction.
The distinction matters under the paper’s photography rules.
A contributor can make a limited colour adjustment to reproduce the scene faithfully.
Adding or removing a person changes what the picture reports.
A record of the editing process helps an editor investigate, but cannot establish on its own what was in front of the camera.
Adobe says Content Credentials can carry information about the creator and how a file was made.
Its management service does not allow deletion of credentials applied to disclose generative AI use.
A photographer choosing software before an assignment has more control over that record than an editor trying to resolve a disputed label afterwards.
